newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: HOCKEY-PAKISTAN SURVIVE DISMISSALS TO DRAW WITH DUTCH.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-PAKISTAN SURVIVE DISMISSALS TO DRAW WITH DUTCH.

text.p: World champions Pakistan drew 3-3 with the Netherlands in the Golden Jubilee of Pakistan tournament on Tuesday despite playing nearly half of a bruising match with less than 11 players.
Three Pakistanis -- Tariq Imran, Muhammad Khalid and Tahir Zaman -- were shown yellow cards which earned them temporary dismissals.

Tariq, one of Pakistan's newcomers, was sent off for half an hour -- one of the longest suspensions in the history of the sport -- for a ninth minute foul off the ball on Dutch captain Stephan Veen. Veen was badly shaken and had to leave the pitch.
The Dutch, the current Olympic champions, took an early lead through Bram Lomans before Pakistan equalised and went ahead through a corner goal from Muhammad Shahbaz and a penalty from Tahir Zaman.
The home side were then reduced to nine men thanks to two suspensions, including that of Tariq, but the Dutch failed to find an equaliser.
It was only when Pakistan had 11 players back on the pitch in the 41st minute that the Netherlands pulled level through another Lomans corner goal.
Muhammad Shahbaz restored Pakistan's lead with his second of the match but with five minutes to go Jaap Buma levelled the scores and earned the Netherlands a point.
Earlier, Germany beat Australia 2-1 with a dramatic winner 10 seconds from time by Christoph Bechmann.
